# `Q-5-56` — Invalid `quarto-required` Value

> `quarto-required` in `_quarto.yml` must be a version range string,
> such as `"^2"`.

## What this means

`quarto-required` holds a version range written as a string, in the
syntax npm uses (`"^2"`, `">=2.1"`, `"2.x"`). This value is not one:
it is a number, a list or another non-string value, an empty string,
or text that is not a range.

```yaml
quarto-required: 2      # Q-5-56: a number, not a string
quarto-required: "two"  # Q-5-56: not a version range
```

Quarto 1 rejects these values too: a non-string value fails its
configuration check.

## How to fix it

For a Quarto 2 project, write:

```yaml
quarto-required: "^2"
```

Quote the range. Unquoted, a bare number such as `2` is read as a
number.

See [Declaring the Quarto version of a project](../../guides/projects/quarto-version.qmd).
